ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Excessive catharsis

A patient taking lactulose for recurrent HE develops eight watery stools daily, orthostatic symptoms and low potassium. His family assumes more diarrhea must mean better protection. Which management principle is most appropriate?

  1. Ignore potassium because it cannot affect HE
  2. Stop every HE medicine permanently without review
  3. Use stool frequency as the sole measure of brain function
  4. Reassess dosing and correct dehydration and electrolyte losses
  5. Increase lactulose until diarrhea is continuous
Answer and explanation

Reassess dosing and correct dehydration and electrolyte losses

Excessive catharsis can cause dehydration and electrolyte abnormalities that themselves worsen HE risk.

Option explanations

Reassess dosing and correct dehydration and electrolyte losses: Excessive catharsis can cause dehydration and electrolyte abnormalities that themselves worsen HE risk.

Increase lactulose until diarrhea is continuous: This may worsen dehydration and electrolyte loss.

Ignore potassium because it cannot affect HE: Electrolyte disturbance can precipitate deterioration.

Stop every HE medicine permanently without review: Treatment should be adjusted rather than abandoned without a plan.

Use stool frequency as the sole measure of brain function: Clinical status and complications matter as well.
